mcqs.question: When a straight conductor carries current upward, the magnetic field at a point to the east of the wire is ___; when the same conductor carries current downward, the magnetic field at the same point is ___ (use the right‑hand thumb rule).

options.A: Into the page, into the page
options.B: Into the page, out of the page
options.C: Out of the page, into the page
options.D: Out of the page, out of the page

mcqs.answer: Into the page, out of the page
mcqs.explanation: Point your right thumb upward (current up); the curled fingers show the magnetic field direction at the east side of the wire as into the page. Reversing the current (thumb down) flips the field direction to out of the page. Hence the correct pair is 'Into the page, out of the page'.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand field around a circular loop
mcqs.question: A circular loop of radius 5 cm carries a current of 3 A. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field at the centre of the loop? (μ₀ = 4π×10⁻⁷ T·m/A)
mcqs.explanation: For a single circular loop, B = μ₀I/(2R). Substituting I=3 A, R=0.05 m gives B = (4π×10⁻⁷ ×3)/(2×0.05) = 12π×10⁻⁶ T ≈ 3.8×10⁻⁵ T. Option A matches this value.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines a magnetic field?

options.A: A region where magnetic forces can be detected, produced by magnets or moving charges.
options.B: A type of electric field produced by static charges.
options.C: The flow of electrons in a conductor.
options.D: A property of materials that makes them conduct electricity.

mcqs.answer: A region where magnetic forces can be detected, produced by magnets or moving charges.
mcqs.explanation: A magnetic field is the space around a magnet or a current‑carrying conductor in which other magnetic materials experience a force. The other options describe unrelated concepts.

mcqs.question: How are magnetic field lines around a straight current‑carrying conductor correctly represented?

options.A: Straight lines radiating outward from the conductor.
options.B: Concentric circles around the conductor, with direction given by the right‑hand rule.
options.C: Random zigzag patterns around the conductor.
options.D: Parallel lines parallel to the conductor.

mcqs.answer: Concentric circles around the conductor, with direction given by the right‑hand rule.
mcqs.explanation: The magnetic field produced by a straight conductor forms closed circular loops centred on the wire. The direction of the field at any point is found using the right‑hand thumb rule. Options A, C, D are incorrect representations.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand field around a straight conductor
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the magnetic field pattern around a straight conductor from that around a bar magnet?

options.A: Both have field lines forming concentric circles.
options.B: Around a straight conductor, field lines are concentric circles; around a bar magnet, field lines emerge from the north pole and enter the south pole.
options.C: Around a straight conductor, field lines go from north to south; around a bar magnet they are circular.
options.D: There is no magnetic field around a straight conductor.

mcqs.answer: Around a straight conductor, field lines are concentric circles; around a bar magnet, field lines emerge from the north pole and enter the south pole.
mcqs.explanation: A straight current‑carrying wire produces circular field lines centred on the wire. A bar magnet’s field lines start at the north pole, curve through space, and end at the south pole, forming closed loops. Option B captures this distinction.

mcqs.question: A current of 5 A flows upward through a vertical wire. What is the direction of the magnetic field at a point located 10 cm due east of the wire?
mcqs.explanation: Point the right thumb upward (direction of current). The curled fingers point into the page on the east side of the wire, indicating the magnetic field direction there. Hence the field is into the page.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand field around a circular loop
mcqs.question: A circular coil of radius 2 cm carries a current of 2 A. Which statement about the magnetic field at a point 1 cm above the centre of the coil is correct?

options.A: The field at the point is zero because it is outside the coil.
options.B: The field is directed along the axis of the coil and its magnitude is greater than at the centre.
options.C: The field is directed along the axis of the coil and its magnitude is less than at the centre.
options.D: The field is perpendicular to the axis and equal in magnitude to that at the centre.

mcqs.answer: The field is directed along the axis of the coil and its magnitude is less than at the centre.
mcqs.explanation: The magnetic field of a circular loop is strongest at its centre and decreases with distance along the axis. At 1 cm above the centre, the field still points along the axis (perpendicular to the plane of the coil) but its magnitude is smaller than the central value. Option C correctly describes this.

mcqs.question: A student places a compass near a straight current‑carrying wire. When the current direction is reversed, the compass needle rotates. Which explanation best describes this observation?

options.A: The compass needle aligns with Earth's magnetic field, unaffected by the wire.
options.B: Reversing the current reverses the magnetic field direction around the wire, causing the compass needle to rotate accordingly.
options.C: The current creates an electric field that pushes the compass needle.
options.D: The wire heats up, causing thermal expansion that moves the compass.

mcqs.answer: Reversing the current reverses the magnetic field direction around the wire, causing the compass needle to rotate accordingly.
mcqs.explanation: According to the right‑hand thumb rule, the direction of the magnetic field produced by a current‑carrying wire depends on the direction of the current. Reversing the current flips the field direction, so the compass needle, which aligns with the local magnetic field, also flips. The other options do not explain the observed rotation.
